N01.name: First Taste of Victory
N01.summary: Win any official victory, including a Time victory.
N01.honor: Your civilization has earned a victory of its own.
N01.clue:
Let your civilization
celebrate its first victory.
N01.condition: Win any official victory, including a Time victory.

N02.name: Pioneer
N02.summary: Found your second city after the capital yourself; conquered or gifted cities do not count.
N02.honor: New walls rise in the distance.
N02.indexClue: Found a new city far from home
N02.clue:
Let a new city rise
beyond your capital.
N02.condition: Found your second city after the capital yourself; conquered or gifted cities do not count.

N03.name: Seeds of Culture
N03.summary: Adopt your first social policy; opening a policy tree also counts.
N03.honor: A civilization's ideas begin with its first choice.
N03.clue:
The ideas of a civilization
begin with a choice.
N03.condition: Adopt your first social policy; opening a policy tree also counts.

N04.name: Festival of Two Cities
N04.summary: During one uninterrupted Golden Age, build at least one World Wonder yourself in each of two different cities you own; the count resets if the Golden Age ends.
N04.honor: Two cities shared the splendor of a Golden Age.
N04.indexClue: Let a Golden Age illuminate two wonders
N04.clue:
During the same Golden Age,
leave a wonder in each of two cities.
N04.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. During one uninterrupted Golden Age, build at least one World Wonder yourself in each of two different cities you own; the count resets if the Golden Age ends.

N05.name: A First Wonder
N05.summary: Build your first World Wonder yourself; Great Engineer assistance is allowed, but National Wonders do not count.
N05.honor: You have left this age its first monument.
N05.clue:
With your own hands,
leave this age a World Wonder.
N05.condition: Build your first World Wonder yourself; Great Engineer assistance is allowed, but National Wonders do not count.

N06.name: First Clash
N06.summary: Destroy an enemy military unit in combat; Barbarians count, but capturing civilians does not.
N06.honor: Your first clash has written a tale of courage.
N06.clue:
Let a true clash of arms
reveal your strength.
N06.condition: Destroy an enemy military unit in combat; Barbarians count, but capturing civilians does not.

N07.name: Frontier Patrol
N07.summary: Use the same military unit to clear Barbarian encampments at 3 different locations. It must still be alive when the third clearance resolves; upgrading preserves its record.
N07.honor: Along the distant frontier, someone keeps watch.
N07.indexClue: Clear three camps with the same unit
N07.clue:
After three Barbarian camps,
bring the same unit home alive.
N07.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Use the same military unit to clear Barbarian encampments at 3 different locations. It must still be alive when the third clearance resolves; upgrading preserves its record.

N08.name: Veteran Conqueror
N08.summary: Use a military unit with at least 3 combat-earned promotions to capture in battle a city founded by another major civilization. It must survive the capture; free promotions do not count.
N08.honor: A veteran's banner now flies over an enemy city.
N08.indexClue: Take a city with a veteran of three promotions
N08.clue:
Let a veteran with three combat promotions
take an enemy city in person.
N08.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Use a military unit with at least 3 combat-earned promotions to capture in battle a city founded by another major civilization. It must survive the capture; free promotions do not count.

N09.name: Working the Land
N09.summary: Have your own Worker build a new Farm, Mine or Pasture; repairing an existing improvement does not count.
N09.honor: The land begins to reward your labor.
N09.indexClue: Cultivate a piece of land yourself
N09.clue:
Let your Worker
change this land for the first time.
N09.condition: Have your own Worker build a new Farm, Mine or Pasture; repairing an existing improvement does not count.

N10.name: All Roads Connected
N10.summary: At turn end, at least 3 cities you founded besides the capital must simultaneously have game-recognized road or harbor connections to the capital; the capital does not count toward the 3.
N10.honor: Roads and sea routes weave your lands together.
N10.indexClue: Connect three founded cities to the capital
N10.clue:
Let three cities you founded
join your capital in one network.
N10.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, at least 3 cities you founded besides the capital must simultaneously have game-recognized road or harbor connections to the capital; the capital does not count toward the 3.

N11.name: A City of Learning
N11.summary: At turn end, a city you founded must have at least 15 population and both a Library and a University.
N11.honor: Knowledge and people gather in one city.
N11.indexClue: Give a city of fifteen a university
N11.clue:
In a city of fifteen,
let a Library and University flourish together.
N11.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, a city you founded must have at least 15 population and both a Library and a University.

N12.name: Trade Brings Gold
N12.summary: At turn end, hold at least 1,000 gold while at least 3 cities you founded each have both a Market and a Bank.
N12.honor: Wealth has firm foundations; prosperity is no accident.
N12.indexClue: Build three trading cities and save a thousand gold
N12.clue:
Let three cities have Markets and Banks,
with a thousand gold in reserve.
N12.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, hold at least 1,000 gold while at least 3 cities you founded each have both a Market and a Bank.

N13.name: City-State Round Table
N13.summary: At turn end, simultaneously be allied with city-states of at least 3 different types; eliminated city-states do not count.
N13.honor: Different city-states gather around the same table.
N13.indexClue: Ally with three types of city-state
N13.clue:
Let three kinds of city-state
choose your alliance together.
N13.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, simultaneously be allied with city-states of at least 3 different types; eliminated city-states do not count.

N14.name: Faith Takes Root
N14.summary: Found a full religion yourself and, at turn end, make it the majority religion in at least 3 cities you founded simultaneously; a Pantheon alone does not count.
N14.honor: Faith has taken root in your lands.
N14.indexClue: Establish your religion in three founded cities
N14.clue:
Let the religion you founded
become the majority in three cities you founded.
N14.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Religion must be enabled. Found a full religion yourself and, at turn end, make it the majority religion in at least 3 cities you founded simultaneously; a Pantheon alone does not count.

N15.name: Treaties of Trade
N15.summary: In one game, complete a valid trade with each of 3 different major civilizations. Each trade must include a positive amount of gold, gold per turn, resources or Open Borders; embassy-only agreements do not count.
N15.honor: Three treaties have opened three borders.
N15.clue:
In a single journey,
exchange what you need with three civilizations.
N15.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. In one game, complete a valid trade with each of 3 different major civilizations. Each trade must include a positive amount of gold, gold per turn, resources or Open Borders; embassy-only agreements do not count.

N16.name: Wonders of Nature
N16.summary: Discover 3 different types of Natural Wonder through exploration in one game; each type counts only once.
N16.honor: Nature's marvels have become part of your story.
N16.indexClue: Discover three types of Natural Wonder
N16.clue:
Journey beyond the horizon
to find three wonders of nature.
N16.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Discover 3 different types of Natural Wonder through exploration in one game; each type counts only once.

N17.name: A Precise Path to the Stars
N17.summary: Win a Scientific victory without ever owning more than 4 cities at once or capturing in battle a city founded by another major civilization during the entire game.
N17.honor: From limited lands, you reached the boundless stars.
N17.indexClue: Reach the stars with at most four cities
N17.clue:
Take no cities in battle; own no more than four.
Let science carry you to victory.
N17.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Win a Scientific victory without ever owning more than 4 cities at once or capturing in battle a city founded by another major civilization during the entire game.

N18.name: A Four-City Masterpiece
N18.summary: Win a Cultural victory without ever owning more than 4 cities at once during the entire game; cities briefly owned and then abandoned still count toward the limit.
N18.honor: A handful of cities has written a civilization's masterpiece.
N18.indexClue: Win through culture with at most four cities
N18.clue:
Keep your realm within four cities
and let culture win the world.
N18.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Win a Cultural victory without ever owning more than 4 cities at once during the entire game; cities briefly owned and then abandoned still count toward the limit.

N19.name: One City's Campaign
N19.summary: Win a Domination victory having founded only your capital throughout the entire game. Capturing other cities is allowed; founding and then abandoning another city is not.
N19.honor: One starting point led to the whole world.
N19.indexClue: Found only one city and conquer the world
N19.clue:
Found just one city yourself,
and set out from there to conquer.
N19.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Win a Domination victory having founded only your capital throughout the entire game. Capturing other cities is allowed; founding and then abandoning another city is not.

N20.name: Diplomacy over Monuments
N20.summary: Win a Diplomatic victory while building no more than 2 different types of World Wonder yourself throughout the entire game; National Wonders do not count.
N20.honor: The world's trust outweighs towering stone.
N20.indexClue: Win through diplomacy with few wonders
N20.clue:
Build no more than two kinds of World Wonder
and win the world through diplomacy.
N20.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Win a Diplomatic victory while building no more than 2 different types of World Wonder yourself throughout the entire game; National Wonders do not count.

N21.name: A Peaceful Metropolis
N21.summary: At turn end, a city you founded must have at least 25 population. Throughout the entire game, never own more than 3 cities at once or capture in battle a city founded by another major civilization.
N21.honor: Restraint in expansion can still light countless homes.
N21.indexClue: Grow a great city without conquest
N21.clue:
Own no more than three cities; take none in battle.
Let one city grow to twenty-five.
N21.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, a city you founded must have at least 25 population. Throughout the entire game, never own more than 3 cities at once or capture in battle a city founded by another major civilization.

N22.name: The Path of Mastery
N22.summary: Fully adopt 2 social policy trees, having never owned more than 3 cities at once in the game up to that moment.
N22.honor: A compact realm carries mature institutions.
N22.indexClue: Complete two policy trees within three cities
N22.clue:
Keep your realm within three cities
and let two policy trees fully bloom.
N22.condition: Prince difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Fully adopt 2 social policy trees, having never owned more than 3 cities at once in the game up to that moment.

N23.name: A Golden Alliance
N23.summary: At turn end, hold at least 3,000 gold and simultaneously have at least 4 allied city-states that have not been eliminated.
N23.honor: Your treasury and treaties sustain your influence together.
N23.clue:
Keep three thousand gold in your treasury
and four city-states at your side.
N23.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, hold at least 3,000 gold and simultaneously have at least 4 allied city-states that have not been eliminated.

N24.name: One Faith, Three Nations
N24.summary: Found and enhance a religion yourself. At turn end, it must be the majority religion in the current capitals of at least 3 different other major civilizations.
N24.honor: Your creed has crossed the capitals of three nations.
N24.indexClue: Bring your faith to three foreign capitals
N24.clue:
Enhance your own religion
and let three foreign capitals embrace it.
N24.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Religion must be enabled. Found and enhance a religion yourself. At turn end, it must be the majority religion in the current capitals of at least 3 different other major civilizations.

N25.name: Guardians of City-States
N25.summary: At turn end, simultaneously have at least 5 allied city-states that have not been eliminated, covering at least 3 city-state types.
N25.honor: Five city-states give the world a shared voice.
N25.clue:
Across three kinds of city-state,
let five allies stand together.
N25.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, simultaneously have at least 5 allied city-states that have not been eliminated, covering at least 3 city-state types.

N26.name: Pilgrimage of Wonders
N26.summary: Build 12 different types of World Wonder yourself across at least 3 new games meeting this achievement's difficulty and opponent requirements. Build at least one type in every counted game; reloading the same game does not add a game.
N26.honor: Across ages and journeys, you left twelve monuments.
N26.indexClue: Build twelve kinds of wonder across three journeys
N26.clue:
Across at least three journeys,
build twelve kinds of World Wonder yourself.
N26.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Build 12 different types of World Wonder yourself across at least 3 new games meeting this achievement's difficulty and opponent requirements. Build at least one type in every counted game; reloading the same game does not add a game.

N27.name: Skyline of the Nile
N27.summary: As Egypt, build 5 different types of World Wonder yourself in the same city, which you must still own; wonders already present when you acquired the city do not count.
N27.honor: Beside the Nile, one city holds a magnificent skyline.
N27.indexClue: Build five kinds of wonder in one Egyptian city
N27.clue:
Let one city of Egypt
build five kinds of World Wonder.
N27.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. As Egypt, build 5 different types of World Wonder yourself in the same city, which you must still own; wonders already present when you acquired the city do not count.

N28.name: Rome's Living Network
N28.summary: As Rome, at turn end, at least 5 cities you founded must each have at least 10 population and a Monument, Granary, Library and Barracks simultaneously.
N28.honor: Rome's strength grows in every city.
N28.indexClue: Let five Roman cities flourish together
N28.clue:
Let five Roman cities each have
ten population and four basic buildings.
N28.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. As Rome, at turn end, at least 5 cities you founded must each have at least 10 population and a Monument, Granary, Library and Barracks simultaneously.

N29.name: Four Cities in Harmony
N29.summary: At turn end, at least 4 cities you founded must each have at least 20 population, your civilization must have at least 10 Happiness, and you must never previously have captured in battle a city founded by another major civilization.
N29.honor: Four flourishing cities are joined by peace and order.
N29.indexClue: Let four great cities prosper in peace
N29.clue:
Expand without taking cities in battle.
Let four cities of twenty thrive in happiness.
N29.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. At turn end, at least 4 cities you founded must each have at least 20 population, your civilization must have at least 10 Happiness, and you must never previously have captured in battle a city founded by another major civilization.

N30.name: City of a Thousand Visions
N30.summary: Build 8 different types of World Wonder yourself in the same city, which you must still own; wonders already present when you acquired the city do not count.
N30.honor: One city holds an entire age's imagination.
N30.indexClue: Gather eight kinds of World Wonder in one city
N30.clue:
Let the same city
build eight kinds of World Wonder.
N30.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. Build 8 different types of World Wonder yourself in the same city, which you must still own; wonders already present when you acquired the city do not count.

N31.name: Home from Battle
N31.summary: The same surviving military unit must earn at least 5 combat promotions and destroy at least 10 military units of major civilizations. Defensive kills count; Barbarians and free promotions do not. Upgrading preserves the record.
N31.honor: A unit returns, carrying memories of countless battles.
N31.indexClue: Bring a veteran of five promotions home alive
N31.clue:
Five combat promotions, ten major-civilization kills.
Bring the same unit home alive.
N31.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. The same surviving military unit must earn at least 5 combat promotions and destroy at least 10 military units of major civilizations. Defensive kills count; Barbarians and free promotions do not. Upgrading preserves the record.

N32.name: Dawn over Three Cities
N32.summary: During the same turn of your own, capture 3 different cities in battle, all founded by other major civilizations. Repeated captures of the same city, trades and direct liberation do not count.
N32.honor: One dawn shines on three new banners.
N32.indexClue: Capture three enemy cities in one turn
N32.clue:
In one turn,
take three different enemy cities.
N32.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. During the same turn of your own, capture 3 different cities in battle, all founded by other major civilizations. Repeated captures of the same city, trades and direct liberation do not count.

N33.name: Faith beyond Borders
N33.summary: Your founded religion must simultaneously be the majority religion in at least 15 cities, including at least 5 belonging to other major civilizations and spanning at least 3 different other major civilizations. Natural spread counts; checked at turn end.
N33.honor: Faith across borders has found a wide welcome.
N33.indexClue: Carry your faith across borders to fifteen cities
N33.clue:
Let the religion you founded
cross borders and become the majority in fifteen cities.
N33.condition: King difficulty or higher; start with at least 3 AI opponents. Religion must be enabled. Your founded religion must simultaneously be the majority religion in at least 15 cities, including at least 5 belonging to other major civilizations and spanning at least 3 different other major civilizations. Natural spread counts; checked at turn end.

N34.name: Legend of the Repeating Crossbow
N34.summary: As China, a Cho-Ko-Nu with at least 4 combat-earned promotions must actively attack and kill 2 different military units of major civilizations during the same turn of your own, and survive to turn end; free promotions and Barbarians do not count.
N34.honor: A seasoned crossbow wrote a legend in one turn.
N34.indexClue: Let a veteran Cho-Ko-Nu score two kills in one turn
N34.clue:
Let a Cho-Ko-Nu with four promotions
kill two major-civilization foes in one turn and survive.
N34.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. As China, a Cho-Ko-Nu with at least 4 combat-earned promotions must actively attack and kill 2 different military units of major civilizations during the same turn of your own, and survive to turn end; free promotions and Barbarians do not count.

N35.name: Persia's Long Day
N35.summary: As Persia, during one uninterrupted Golden Age, capture 4 different cities in battle whose founders include at least 2 other major civilizations. Extending the Golden Age counts; the count resets if it ends.
N35.honor: The long day of a Golden Age witnessed a campaign across nations.
N35.indexClue: Take four cities in Persia's long day
N35.clue:
Let Persia's Golden Age witness
a four-city campaign across two civilizations.
N35.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. As Persia, during one uninterrupted Golden Age, capture 4 different cities in battle whose founders include at least 2 other major civilizations. Extending the Golden Age counts; the count resets if it ends.

N36.name: A Small Nation's Triumph
N36.summary: Win a victory other than Time without ever owning more than 3 cities at once or capturing in battle a city founded by another major civilization during the entire game.
N36.honor: A small nation has room for a great victory.
N36.indexClue: Triumph with at most three cities
N36.clue:
Own no more than three cities; take none in battle.
Win a victory other than Time.
N36.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. Win a victory other than Time without ever owning more than 3 cities at once or capturing in battle a city founded by another major civilization during the entire game.

N37.name: Victory against the Gods
N37.summary: Win a victory other than Time; Scientific, Cultural, Domination and Diplomatic victories all count.
N37.honor: From the hardest beginning, you found your way to victory.
N37.clue:
Begin on Deity difficulty
and win a victory other than Time.
N37.condition: Deity difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. Win a victory other than Time; Scientific, Cultural, Domination and Diplomatic victories all count.

N38.name: One City among the Stars
N38.summary: Enable One City Challenge and win a Scientific victory without ever owning more than 1 city at once during the entire game; even briefly acquiring a second city disqualifies the game.
N38.honor: One city sent its banner to the stars.
N38.indexClue: Reach the stars in One City Challenge
N38.clue:
In One City Challenge,
let your only city win a Scientific victory.
N38.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. Enable One City Challenge and win a Scientific victory without ever owning more than 1 city at once during the entire game; even briefly acquiring a second city disqualifies the game.

N39.name: Culture without Wonders
N39.summary: Win a Cultural victory without ever owning any World Wonder throughout the entire game, including wonders in conquered or acquired cities; National Wonders are unrestricted.
N39.honor: Even without World Wonders, your civilization is remembered.
N39.indexClue: Win through culture without owning World Wonders
N39.clue:
Never own a single World Wonder.
Let culture itself carry you to victory.
N39.condition: Emperor difficulty or higher; start with at least 4 AI opponents. Win a Cultural victory without ever owning any World Wonder throughout the entire game, including wonders in conquered or acquired cities; National Wonders are unrestricted.

N40.name: The Complete Chronicle
N40.summary: Complete the other 39 achievements in this preview catalog.
N40.honor: Every road has left a chapter in your civilization.
N40.clue:
Travel the other thirty-nine roads
and write the final page.
N40.condition: Complete the other 39 achievements in this preview catalog.
